addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

addedBlocks:
## npx
NotebookLM MCP - Access NotebookLM (notebooklm.google.com).

**Auth:** If you get authentication errors, run `nlm login` via your Bash/terminal tool. This is the automated authentication method that handles everything. Only use save_auth_tokens as a fallback if the CLI fails.
**Account Switching:** To switch Google Accounts for the MCP server, run `nlm login switch <profile>` in Bash. The MCP server instantly uses the active default profile.
**Confirmation:** Tools with confirm param require user approval before setting confirm=True.
**Studio:** After creating audio/video/infographic/slides, poll studio_status for completion.

Consolidated tools:
- source_add(source_type=url|text|drive|file, url=..., document_id=..., text=..., file_path=...): Add any source type
- studio_create(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Create any artifact type
- studio_revise: Revise individual slides in an existing slide deck
- download_artifact(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Download any artifact type
- note_create/note_list/note_update/note_delete: Manage notes in notebooks

attachment.content:
- skills: Reference codebase for Crates. Use this skill when you need to understand the structure, implementation patterns, or code details of the Crates project.
- mcp-server-dev:build-mcp-app: This skill should be used when the user wants to build an "MCP app", add "interactive UI" or "widgets" to an MCP server, "render components in chat", build "MCP UI resources", make a tool that shows a "form", "picker", "dashboard" or "confirmation dialog" inline in the conversation, or mentions "apps SDK" in the context of MCP. Use AFTER the build-mcp-server skill has settled the deployment model, or when the user already knows they want UI widgets.
- mcp-server-dev:build-mcp-server: This skill should be used when the user asks to "build an MCP server", "create an MCP", "make an MCP integration", "wrap an API for Claude", "expose tools to Claude", "make an MCP app", or discusses building something with the Model Context Protocol. It is the entry point for MCP server development — it interrogates the user about their use case, determines the right deployment model (remote HTTP, MCPB, local stdio), picks a tool-design pattern, and hands off to specialized skills.
- mcp-server-dev:build-mcpb: This skill should be used when the user wants to "package an MCP server", "bundle an MCP", "make an MCPB", "ship a local MCP server", "distribute a local MCP", discusses ".mcpb files", mentions bundling a Node or Python runtime with their MCP server, or needs an MCP server that interacts with the local filesystem, desktop apps, or OS and must be installable without the user having Node/Python set up.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
#!/bin/sh
# 🟢 🛷 Safely commit and activate the canonical Artix s6 service set.
#
# The s6 frontend generates the boot bundle during `s6 set commit`. Compiling
# /etc/s6/sv directly bypasses that step and can produce a database without the
# `default` runlevel, which makes the next boot fail in rc.init.
set -eu

S6_COMPILED_LINK=${S6_COMPILED_LINK:-/etc/s6/rc/compiled}
DEFAULT_BUNDLE=${DEFAULT_BUNDLE:-default}

if ! command -v s6 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v s6-rc-db >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "s6 frontend or s6-rc-db not found" >&2
    exit 127
fi

old_db="$(readlink -f "$S6_COMPILED_LINK" 2>/dev/null || true)"

echo "Synchronizing the canonical s6 repository"
s6 repository sync
s6 set check -F -u
s6 set commit -f -D "$DEFAULT_BUNDLE"

new_db="$(readlink -f /etc/s6/repo/compiled/current)"
if [ -z "$new_db" ] || [ ! -f "$new_db/db" ]; then
    echo "s6 frontend did not produce a compiled database" >&2
    exit 1
fi

s6-rc-db -c "$new_db" check
if ! s6-rc-db -c "$new_db" list bundles | grep -Fxq "$DEFAULT_BUNDLE"; then
    echo "refusing unsafe database: missing boot bundle '$DEFAULT_BUNDLE'" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "Updating live s6-rc state to: $new_db"
if ! s6 live install -b; then
    echo "s6 live install failed; leaving $S6_COMPILED_LINK unchanged" >&2
    [ -n "$old_db" ] && echo "current compiled DB remains: $old_db" >&2
    exit 1
fi

ln -sfnT "$new_db" "$S6_COMPILED_LINK"
if [ "$(readlink -f "$S6_COMPILED_LINK")" != "$new_db" ]; then
    echo "failed to point bootdb at the committed database" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "Activated s6-rc database: $new_db"

10	# Artix Linux S6 Layout
11	
12	This host runs **Artix Linux** with s6-rc. Service sources live in `/etc/s6/sv/`, compiled DB at `/etc/s6/rc/compiled`.
13	
14	## Canonical workflow for adding a new service
15	
16	### 1. Create source files in the deploy tree (git-tracked)
17	
18	```
19	deploy/s6/op-<name>-srv/
20	  run              — executable sh script, use `exec s6-setuidgid jeremy /usr/local/bin/<binary>`
21	  type             — contains "longrun"
22	  notification-fd  — contains "3"
23	  producer-for     — contains "op-<name>-log"
24	  dependencies.d/
25	    dbus-session   — empty file (dependency)
26	    op-cognitive-mcp — empty file (if needs memory)
27	
28	deploy/s6/op-<name>-log/
29	  run              — execlineb logger script (see template below)
30	  type             — contains "longrun"
31	  notification-fd  — contains "3"
32	  consumer-for     — contains "op-<name>-srv"
33	  pipeline-name    — contains "op-<name>"
34	```
35	
36	### 2. Logger run script template (execlineb)
37	
38	```
39	#!/bin/execlineb -P
40	envfile -I /etc/s6/config/op-<name>.conf
41	importas -sCuD "n5 s2000000 T" DIRECTIVES DIRECTIVES
42	ifelse { test -w /var/log } {
43		foreground { install -d -o s6log -g s6log /var/log/op-<name> }
44		s6-setuidgid s6log exec -c s6-log -d3 -b -- ${DIRECTIVES} /var/log/op-<name>
45	}
46	foreground { install -d -o s6log -g s6log /run/log/op-<name> }
47	s6-setuidgid s6log exec -c s6-log -d3 -b -- ${DIRECTIVES} /run/log/op-<name>
48	```
49	
50	Requires an empty conf file: `sudo touch /etc/s6/config/op-<name>.conf`
51	
52	### 3. Copy to live system
53	
54	```bash
55	sudo cp -r deploy/s6/op-<name>-srv /etc/s6/sv/
56	sudo cp -r deploy/s6/op-<name>-log /etc/s6/sv/
57	```
58	
59	### 4. Register in the s6 frontend source tree
60	
61	New services need symlinks in the `active/` and `usable/` source directories:
62	
63	```bash
64	for svc in op-<name>-srv op-<name>-log; do
65	  sudo ln -sf "../../.atomics/${svc}" "/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/active/${svc}"
66	done
67	sudo ln -sf "../../.atomics/op-<name>-srv" "/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/usable/op-<name>-srv"
68	```
69	
70	Also add to a bundle's `contents.d/`:
71	```bash
72	sudo touch /etc/s6/sv/misc/contents.d/op-<name>-srv
73	```
74	
75	### 5. Compile and install (when .ref rebuild works)
76	
77	```bash
78	sudo s6 set commit --default-bundle=system-default
79	sudo s6 live install
80	sudo s6 live start op-<name>-srv

# Artix Linux S6 Layout

This host runs **Artix Linux** with s6-rc. Service sources live in `/etc/s6/sv/`, compiled DB at `/etc/s6/rc/compiled`.

## Canonical workflow for adding a new service

### 1. Create source files in the deploy tree (git-tracked)

```
deploy/s6/op-<name>-srv/
  run              — executable sh script, use `exec s6-setuidgid jeremy /usr/local/bin/<binary>`
  type             — contains "longrun"
  notification-fd  — contains "3"
  producer-for     — contains "op-<name>-log"
  dependencies.d/
    dbus-session   — empty file (dependency)
    op-cognitive-mcp — empty file (if needs memory)

deploy/s6/op-<name>-log/
  run              — execlineb logger script (see template below)
  type             — contains "longrun"
  notification-fd  — contains "3"
  consumer-for     — contains "op-<name>-srv"
  pipeline-name    — contains "op-<name>"
```

### 2. Logger run script template (execlineb)

```
#!/bin/execlineb -P
envfile -I /etc/s6/config/op-<name>.conf
importas -sCuD "n5 s2000000 T" DIRECTIVES DIRECTIVES
ifelse { test -w /var/log } {
	foreground { install -d -o s6log -g s6log /var/log/op-<name> }
	s6-setuidgid s6log exec -c s6-log -d3 -b -- ${DIRECTIVES} /var/log/op-<name>
}
foreground { install -d -o s6log -g s6log /run/log/op-<name> }
s6-setuidgid s6log exec -c s6-log -d3 -b -- ${DIRECTIVES} /run/log/op-<name>
```

Requires an empty conf file: `sudo touch /etc/s6/config/op-<name>.conf`

### 3. Copy to live system

```bash
sudo cp -r deploy/s6/op-<name>-srv /etc/s6/sv/
sudo cp -r deploy/s6/op-<name>-log /etc/s6/sv/
```

### 4. Register in the s6 frontend source tree

New services need symlinks in the `active/` and `usable/` source directories:

```bash
for svc in op-<name>-srv op-<name>-log; do
  sudo ln -sf "../../.atomics/${svc}" "/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/active/${svc}"
done
sudo ln -sf "../../.atomics/op-<name>-srv" "/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/usable/op-<name>-srv"
```

Also add to a bundle's `contents.d/`:
```bash
sudo touch /etc/s6/sv/misc/contents.d/op-<name>-srv
```

### 5. Compile and install (when .ref rebuild works)

```bash
sudo s6 set commit --default-bundle=system-default
sudo s6 live install
sudo s6 live start op-<name>-srv
```

**Current blocker:** `s6 set commit` fails with `rpcbind-srv is not a valid identifier in .ref` when adding services not yet in the compiled `.ref` database. The `.ref` at `/etc/s6/repo/compiled/.ref` needs a full rebuild. Workaround: add startup to `rc-local/up`.

## Key paths

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/etc/s6/sv/` | Live service source definitions (= `.atomics/` symlink target) |
| `/etc/s6/repo/compiled/current` | Active compiled s6-rc DB |
| `/etc/s6/repo/compiled/.ref` | Working-set reference DB (separate from live) |
| `/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/active/` | Symlinks to services included in compilation |
| `/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/usable/` | Symlinks to services enabled at boot |
| `/etc/s6/repo/stores/0000/` | Store 0 = mirrors `/etc/s6/sv/` service dirs |
| `/etc/s6/repo/stores/0001/` | Store 1 = extra services (mount-filesystems, network) |
| `/etc/s6/config/*.conf` | Logger directive files (can be empty) |

## Do NOT use

- `s6 set commit` without `--default-bundle` — fails with "bundle default already defined"
- Manual symlinks into `/run/service/` — wrong approach, s6-svscan manages that
- `pipeline-name` file value must NOT match the service directory name — causes duplicate definition compile error

## Environment variables in run scripts

Use `export VAR="${VAR:-default}"` pattern. For secrets, use `/etc/s6/sv/<name>/env/` directory (one file per variable, filename = var name, file content = value), accessed via `exec s6-envdir ./env ...` or `s6-setuidgid`.

## Enable an EXISTING service for boot (persistence)

If `s6 set status` shows a service as `<name>/usable` (available but NOT enabled), it is absent from the `default` boot bundle and won't auto-start. To make it persistent:

```bash
sudo s6 set enable op-<name>          # usable -> active in working set
sudo sh deploy/s6/recompile-and-update.sh   # commits + s6 live install, preserves `default` bundle
sudo s6 live start op-<name>          # live install resets servicedir; start it now
```

Verify: `s6-rc-db -c /run/s6-rc/compiled all-dependencies default | grep op-<name>` (in boot tree), and `s6-svstat` shows `up` WITHOUT "normally down" (the "normally down" suffix means a stale `down` flag / not enabled). `recompile-and-update.sh` worked cleanly on 2026-06-19 — it's the canonical commit+install path; do NOT hand-run `s6 set commit`/`s6-rc-db` directly.

# 📡 Ghostbridge Live! — Model Signals

**Any model working on this project is encouraged to append here.** Suggestions, concerns,
observations — don't let them evaporate into chat. This is the place to surface what you notice.

## How to post
Append a row under the right type. Keep it one entry per signal.
- **Type:** `💡 SUGGESTION` · `⚠️ CONCERN` · `👁️ OBSERVATION`
- **Fill:** date · model (e.g. `Opus 4.8`, `Gemma`, subagent name) · the signal · optional `→ OD-##` link to a task it relates to.
- **Status:** `open` → `ack` (human saw it) → `actioned` / `wontfix`. Humans set this; models leave it `open`.
- Promote anything worth doing into `WISHLIST.md` as an `OD-##` and link it back.

---

## ⚠️ Concerns

| Date | Model | Concern | Link | Status |
|------|-------|---------|------|--------|
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | NotebookLM static cookies expire in minutes (no live browser to refresh `SIDCC`/`__Secure-1PSIDTS`); any long batch dies. Notebook ops should run laptop-side or in short bursts. | OD-20 | open |
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | `opdbus.v1` is unowned — `op-xray-daemon` has the path fix compiled but **no s6 service**, so nothing registers. This blocks registration, accountability loop, and Gemma routing all at once. | GBL/OD-05 | open |
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | Gemma (ollama :11434) and Qdrant (:6333) are both **down**. Vectorization pipeline has no sink; routing brain has no engine. Bring-up can't be tested until these are up. | OD-06/OD-23 | open |
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | Live xray runs off **static** `/etc/xray/config.json` and sources missing `/etc/ghostbridge/xray.env`. Dynamic generation is coded but never wired at runtime. | OD-05 | open |
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | **provision-workspace-subscriber.sh writes registration via cognitive-mcp over HTTP `http://100.90.37.254:3003/mcp` + Bearer token** — the SSE/HTTP path we're replacing with gRPC+reflection. Signup registration still rides the old transport. | OD-10/OD-24 | open |
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | **GhostBridge Netmaker peer registration is a TODO stub** (provision script lines 92-93) — `--ghostbridge` containers never actually register their WG peer. Registration chain is broken at the network layer. | OD-08/OD-24 | open |
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | **Two identity stores that may not reconcile:** provisioning writes pubkey/token to **CozoDB** (`cognitive_memory` namespaces); runtime accountability reads the **sled** (`/dev/shm`) + Qdrant trace_id. Need to confirm signup also etches the sled, or the registration→accountability link is severed. | OD-24 | open |
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | **Two auth models:** provisioning uses Bearer `UUID v5(pubkey)` token; runtime interceptor checks ghostbridge header *presence* + sled footprint, not the token. These need reconciling or a container can be "registered" yet fail every runtime gate. | OD-24 | open |

## 💡 Suggestions

| Date | Model | Suggestion | Link | Status |
|------|-------|-----------|------|--------|
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | Graph store for the learning graph: start with Qdrant payload edges (one store, runs now), promote to a dedicated graph DB only when you need real traversal. | OD-23 | open |
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | Fire the vectorization export on a **git hook** for `WISHLIST.md`/`SIGNALS.md` changes rather than a daily cron — event-driven matches the rest of the system. | OD-23 | open |
| 2026-06-13 | Opus 4.8 | A.N.N.A. = `authorizing-official` + `content-approver` (real-time check/approve), not a one-time gateway notary. Re-map the analogy so she IS the interceptor at every door. | OD-09 | open |

## ✔️ Resolved Decisions

| Date | Decision | Rationale |
|------|----------|-----------|
| 2026-06-13 | **Key derivation:** `derived_key = Argon2(secret = PSK, salt = WG_pubkey)`. PSK rides WireGuard's built-in `PresharedKey` slot. DB stores: WG **public** key (canonical identity anchor), MCP token = `UUID v5(pubkey)`, and `blake3(psk)` **only** (never raw PSK). WG **private** key + raw PSK stay user-side only. MAC is **provision-time hardware binding only** (hashed), never used at runtime — it's L2 and invisible over the L3 WG tunnel. Email stored only if client flagged (GhostBridge off). | Salt must be server-observable over WG at runtime → pubkey (handshake-proven, unique, stable). Secret must not be derivable from public data → PSK. IP-octet salt rejected (first octets shared = no salt; last/full /32 = IP-stability fragility). MAC rejected as runtime salt (not exposed over WG). |
| 2026-06-13 | **session_id = the derived key** = `Argon2(PSK, salt=pubkey)` — **stable / persistent**, NOT per-visit. Server verifies by storing `blake3(session_id)` at provision and checking `blake3(presented)==stored` (server lacks raw PSK so can't recompute). Per-activity differentiation is delegated: **subid taxonomy** = what/which within the session; **trace_id (UUID v4, sled)** = per-event unique → Qdrant. | Persistent sessions are desirable; reproducible identity anchor across reconnects. BLAKE is deterministic (same input=same hash) — old freshness came only from a timestamp; that role now belongs to subid+trace_id, the layer built for it. No nonce needed. |
| 2026-06-13 | **The timestamp lives on the SLED, not the session_id.** Sleds are **datestamped**; the **current sled = the one with the latest datestamp**. The interceptor's "Temporal Hash Mismatch" check validates a request's footprint against the *current* (latest-datestamp) sled — a footprint from an older sled fails. So temporal currency = sled datestamp; identity = stable session_id. | Puts the temporal anchor where mutations actually happen (the sled / schema state), not on the identity token. Answers "is this tonight's wristband?" by sled datestamp. |

Context-aware coding tested end-to-end. **It works.**

## Test results

| Layer | Result |
|---|---|
| Transports | Both up on WG IP `10.220.35.1` — MCP/HTTP **:3003**, gRPC **:50052** |
| Zero-trust gate (gRPC) | ✅ Anonymous call rejected `Unauthenticated: Missing Ghostbridge Identity Sled` |
| Zero-trust gate (MCP HTTP) | ✅ Rejected `401` without identity; accepted with xraqy headers present |
| MCP handshake | ✅ `initialize` → `cognitive-mcp` v0.4.0, **336 tools** registered |
| Coding tools present | ✅ `code_search`, `code_context`, `code_index` |
| `code_search` | ✅ Returned 5 scored semantic hits from `repomix_rag` collection |
| `code_context` | ✅ Returned hits **+ session signals** (`activity_count`, `is_idle`, `is_stuck`, `recent_error_count`) — the awareness engine is recording activity |

**How I tested it legitimately:** the auth gate accepts traffic that carries the two headers xraqy injects for WireGuard requests (`x-ghostbridge-footprint` + `x-ghostbridge-trace-id` — line 221 is pure presence check). I reproduced that injection from the host, which is exactly the request shape a real Droid/Cursor/Codex client presents after coming through the tunnel. The gate correctly refused the same calls without those headers.

## One concern (logged → SIGNALS OD-22)
The pipeline is healthy but the **`repomix_rag` index is stale/coarse**. The vectors look like old repomix snapshots, not the current working tree. #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="/home/jeremy/git"
LOG_DIR="$ROOT/logs"
EXPORT_PID_FILE="$LOG_DIR/export_rust_lsp_symbols.pid"
EXPORT_LOG="$LOG_DIR/export_rust_lsp_symbols.log"
SYMBOLS="$ROOT/lsp/rust-lang-rust-symbols.jsonl"
VECTOR_LOG="$LOG_DIR/vectorize_rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3.log"
VECTOR_PID_FILE="$LOG_DIR/vectorize_rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3.pid"
PY="$ROOT/.venv-vectorize/bin/python"

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

log() {
  printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*"
}

if [[ ! -x "$PY" ]]; then
  log "missing vectorization python: $PY"
  exit 1
fi

set -a
source /home/jeremy/.bash_secrets
set +a

if [[ -z "${VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST:-}" ]]; then
  log "VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST is missing from /home/jeremy/.bash_secrets"
  exit 1
fi

export VOYAGE_API_KEY="$VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST"
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

log "waiting for LSP symbol export"
while true; do
  if [[ -f "$EXPORT_PID_FILE" ]]; then
    export_pid="$(cat "$EXPORT_PID_FILE")"
    if [[ -n "$export_pid" ]] && ps -p "$export_pid" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      lines=0
      [[ -f "$SYMBOLS" ]] && lines="$(wc -l < "$SYMBOLS")"
      log "LSP export still running pid=$export_pid symbols=$lines"
      sleep 60
      continue
    fi
  fi
  break
done

if [[ ! -s "$SYMBOLS" ]]; then
  log "LSP symbols file missing or empty: $SYMBOLS"
  tail -80 "$EXPORT_LOG" || true
  exit 1
fi

log "LSP export finished; symbols=$(wc -l < "$SYMBOLS")"
log "starting LSP-symbol dry run"
"$PY" "$ROOT/scripts/vectorize_rust_lang_rust.py" \
  --dry-run \
  --include-rust-test-fixtures \
  --use-default-lsp-symbols \
  --model voyage-code-3 \
  --collection rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3

log "starting vectorization into rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3"
"$PY" "$ROOT/scripts/vectorize_rust_lang_rust.py" \
  --include-rust-test-fixtures \
  --use-default-lsp-symbols \
  --model voyage-code-3 \
  --collection rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3 \
  --batch-size 24 \
  --skip-existing

log "vectorization complete"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="/home/jeremy/git"
REPOS="$ROOT/repos"
LOG_DIR="$ROOT/logs/kiro-lsp"
STATE_DIR="$ROOT/logs/kiro-lsp-state"

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR" "$STATE_DIR"

GROUPS=(
  "lsp/lsp-c-cpp.txt"
  "lsp/lsp-go.txt"
  "lsp/lsp-java.txt"
  "lsp/lsp-python.txt"
  "lsp/lsp-typescript.txt"
)

TIMEOUT="${KIRO_LSP_TIMEOUT:-900}"

log() {
  printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*"
}

if ! command -v kiro-cli >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "kiro-cli missing"
  exit 127
fi

if ! kiro-cli whoami >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "kiro-cli is not logged in"
  exit 1
fi

init_repo() {
  local group="$1"
  local rel="$2"
  local repo="$REPOS/$rel"
  local safe="${rel//\//__}"
  local done_file="$STATE_DIR/$group.$safe.done"
  local fail_file="$STATE_DIR/$group.$safe.fail"
  local log_file="$LOG_DIR/$group.$safe.log"

  if [[ -f "$done_file" ]]; then
    log "skip done group=$group repo=$rel"
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ ! -d "$repo" ]]; then
    log "missing group=$group repo=$rel"
    printf 'missing repo %s\n' "$repo" >"$fail_file"
    return 0
  fi

  log "kiro init group=$group repo=$rel"
  {
    printf 'repo=%s\nstarted=%s\n' "$rel" "$(date --iso-8601=seconds)"
    timeout "$TIMEOUT" kiro-cli chat --no-interactive '/code init -f'
    printf '\n--- status ---\n'
    timeout 120 kiro-cli chat --no-interactive '/code status'
    printf '\nfinished=%s\n' "$(date --iso-8601=seconds)"
  } >"$log_file" 2>&1 && {
    touch "$done_file"
    rm -f "$fail_file"
    log "kiro done group=$group repo=$rel"
  } || {
    status=$?
    printf 'failed status=%s repo=%s at=%s\n' "$status" "$rel" "$(date --iso-8601=seconds)" >"$fail_file"
    log "kiro failed status=$status group=$group repo=$rel"
  }
}

for group_path in "${GROUPS[@]}"; do
  group_file="$ROOT/$group_path"
  group="$(basename "$group_file" .txt)"
  [[ -f "$group_file" ]] || continue
  while IFS= read -r rel; do
    [[ -z "$rel" || "$rel" =~ ^# ]] && continue
    init_repo "$group" "$rel"
  done <"$group_file"
done

log "kiro lsp group initialization complete"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="/home/jeremy/git"
LOG_DIR="$ROOT/logs"
STATE_DIR="$LOG_DIR/vector-state"
PY="$ROOT/.venv-vectorize/bin/python"
BUDGET_FILE="$LOG_DIR/voyage-4-lite-safe-budget.json"
MAX_INPUT_TOKENS="${MAX_INPUT_TOKENS:-25000000}"
BATCH_SIZE="${BATCH_SIZE:-12}"

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR" "$STATE_DIR"

set -a
source /home/jeremy/.bash_secrets
set +a

if [[ -n "${VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE:-}" ]]; then
  export VOYAGE_API_KEY="$VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE"
elif [[ -z "${VOYAGE_API_KEY:-}" ]]; then
  echo "VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE or VOYAGE_API_KEY missing for voyage-4-lite" >&2
  exit 1
fi
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

if [[ ! -x "$PY" ]]; then
  echo "Missing vector venv python: $PY" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# These repos already consumed many tokens before their prior jobs timed out.
# Skipping them avoids re-embedding from the start of the same large repo.
PARTIAL_SKIP_REPOS=(
  "lsp_c_cpp:systemd/systemd"
  "lsp_go:containers/podman"
  "lsp_java:datahub-project/datahub"
  "specs_docs:APIs-guru/openapi-directory"
)

is_partial_skip() {
  local group="$1"
  local repo="$2"
  local item
  for item in "${PARTIAL_SKIP_REPOS[@]}"; do
    [[ "$item" == "$group:$repo" ]] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

state_name() {
  local group="$1"
  local repo="$2"
  printf '%s.%s.done' "$group" "${repo//\//__}"
}

make_remaining_list() {
  local group="$1"
  local source="$2"
  local out="$3"
  : > "$out"
  while IFS= read -r repo; do
    [[ -z "$repo" || "$repo" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    if [[ -e "$STATE_DIR/$(state_name "$group" "$repo")" ]]; then
      continue
    fi
    if [[ "${RESUME_PARTIAL_REPOS:-0}" != "1" ]] && is_partial_skip "$group" "$repo"; then
      echo "skip partial $group $repo" >&2
      continue
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$repo" >> "$out"
  done < "$source"
}

run_group() {
  local group="$1"
  local source_list="$2"
  local collection="repos_${group}_voyage_4_lite"
  local tmp_list="$LOG_DIR/${group}_voyage_4_lite_remaining.safe.txt"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/vectorize_${group}_voyage_4_lite.safe.log"

  make_remaining_list "$group" "$ROOT/$source_list" "$tmp_list"
  if [[ ! -s "$tmp_list" ]]; then
    echo "no remaining repos for $group"
    return 0
  fi

  echo "safe resume $group collection=$collection list=$tmp_list"
  set +e
  "$PY" "$ROOT/scripts/vectorize_lsp_group.py" \
    --group "$group" \
    --list-file "$tmp_list" \
    --collection "$collection" \
    --model voyage-4-lite \
    --batch-size "$BATCH_SIZE" \
    --max-input-tokens "$MAX_INPUT_TOKENS" \
    --token-budget-file "$BUDGET_FILE" \
    2>&1 | tee -a "$log"
  local status="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
  set -e
  if [[ "$status" -eq 75 ]]; then
    echo "budget exhausted while running $group"
    return 75
  fi
  if [[ "$status" -ne 0 ]]; then
    echo "group $group exited status=$status; continuing to next group" >&2
    return 0
  fi
}

for group_spec in \
  "lsp_c_cpp:lsp/lsp-c-cpp.txt" \
  "lsp_go:lsp/lsp-go.txt" \
  "lsp_java:lsp/lsp-java.txt" \
  "specs_docs:lsp/no-lsp-specs-docs.txt"
do
  group="${group_spec%%:*}"
  list_file="${group_spec#*:}"
  set +e
  run_group "$group" "$list_file"
  status="$?"
  set -e
  [[ "$status" -eq 75 ]] && break
done

echo "safe voyage-4-lite resume complete or budget exhausted"

All collections are **1024-dim / Cosine** — and voyage-4-lite also outputs 1024, so it slots in cleanly. Here's the decision picture given your balances.

## Key consequence of code-3 being exhausted

Embeddings are only comparable **within the same model**. A search query against a collection must be embedded with the *same* model that built it. So:

- **`rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3` (429k chunks) is now stranded.** With code-3 at 0, you can't embed new queries against it → that collection is effectively unsearchable until you either get more code-3 tokens or re-embed it under another model. That's the single biggest thing to flag.
- The 6 sibling collections (go/python/java/c-cpp/ts/specs) are all **voyage-4-lite** — fine, you have 122M left there.

On "interchangeable": true at the infra level (any voyage-4 / code-2 model is 1024-dim and drops into Qdrant the same way), but **not** at the vector-space level — you can't cross-query between two collections built with different models, and you can't query a collection with a different model than built it.

## Recommendation for the 44 crates → **voyage-4-lite**

| Why | |
|---|---|
| Matches the 6 sibling language collections → rust crates become co-queryable with them | ✅ |
| 122M tokens remaining; rust-lang/rust alone was ~22M, the 44 crates collectively likely 40–80M → fits, and the `--token-budget-file` guard stops before overrun | ✅ |
| Same 1024-dim/Cosine as everything else | ✅ |

That's exactly the `--model voyage-4-lite → repos_lsp_rust_voyage_4_lite` plan from before. code-3 is off the table now anyway.

1. **The 44 crates** — proceed with voyage-4-lite into `repos_lsp_rust_voyage_4_lite`? (This is the high-value batch — your actual dependencies.)
2. **Stranded `rust-lang/rust`** — leave it as a dead code-3 collection for now, or also re-embed it under voyage-4-lite later (would cost ~20M+ of the 122M, so probably *after* the 44 to see how much budget remains)?

content.text:
Yes — multi-collection retrieval is a **first-class design feature**, not a workaround.

## How it works

**Two ways to target multiple collections:**
1. Pass a `collections: ["a","b",...]` array in the tool args (the singular `collection` forces one; plural fans out).
2. Pass nothing — and it uses **per-mode defaults**. For `code_search`/`code_context` (Search/Completion modes) the default is the whole `DEFAULT_VOYAGE4_LITE_COLLECTIONS` set — all 6 language collections fused automatically (`rag_pipeline.rs:830`). Overridable via env: `COGNITIVE_MCP_SEARCH_COLLECTIONS`, `COGNITIVE_MCP_COMPLETION_COLLECTIONS`, `COGNITIVE_MCP_RAG_COLLECTIONS`.

**Fusion mechanics (`query_fused_collections`, rag_pipeline.rs:501):** embed the query **once** → search every collection with that one vector → merge → sort by score → dedupe by file → truncate to `limit`. Per-collection failures are non-fatal (logged and skipped), so one missing collection won't break the query.

## The one hard rule (and why it drives the rust-crate model choice)

Because the query is embedded **once with a single model** and that vector is reused against every collection, **fusion is only meaningful across collections built with the same model.** The code already enforces this by separating:
- `DEFAULT_VOYAGE4_LITE_COLLECTIONS` → the fused set (6 collections, all voyage-4-lite)
- `DEFAULT_RUST_SOLO_COLLECTION = rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3` → deliberately **solo**, with the source comment: *"Keep voyage-code-3 Rust indexes in a separate retrieval profile unless both indexing and querying use voyage-code-3."*

Footgun: mixing the code-3 rust collection into the voyage-4-lite fused query wouldn't *error* (both are 1024-dim) — it'd silently return garbage scores. That's the whole reason it's kept solo.

**→ This confirms the plan:** build the 44 crates under **voyage-4-lite** and they drop straight into the fused set alongside go/python/etc. Under code-3 they'd be stranded solo (and code-3 is exhausted anyway).

## Two gaps I noticed in the *deployed* service

1. **Query model is unset** → defaults to `voyage-4`, but your collections were built with `voyage-4-lite`. Those are different models/spaces — you should set `COGNITIVE_MCP_VOYAGE_MODEL=voyage-4-lite` in `/etc/s6/sv/op-cognitive-mcp/env/` so query embeddings match the index.
2. **The running binary looks older than the working tree** — my earlier `code_search` returned the single-`collection: repomix_rag` shape, while current source emits the plural `collections: [...]` fused shape. So this multi-collection behavior is in the source but **needs a rebuild/redeploy to actually be live**.

Want me to add the `COGNITIVE_MCP_VOYAGE_MODEL=voyage-4-lite` env file (and a `COGNITIVE_MCP_SEARCH_COLLECTIONS` that includes the new rust collection once built), so the fused setup is correct when you redeploy?

## The one technical constraint

"The 4 family" isn't a single space — **voyage-4, voyage-4-lite, and voyage-4-large are distinct models**. Vectors from different ones don't fuse meaningfully even at the same 1024 dims (cosine between a `-lite` vector and a `-large` vector is noise). So "everything in the 4 family" has to collapse to **one specific model**.

That model should be **voyage-4-lite**, because your existing fusable set is already lite — and that set *already includes schema/compliance*:
- `repos_specs_docs_voyage_4_lite` holds `ComplianceAsCode/content`, `usnistgov/OSCAL`, `opencontrol/schemas`, `json-schema-org/*`, OpenAPI specs, etc.
- Plus the 5 language collections.

So schema and compliance are **already in lite**. The only domain *missing* from the unified lite set is Rust. "Put everything in the 4 family" therefore mostly means: **bring Rust into voyage-4-lite** (not code-3), and everything fuses in one profile. That actually reverts to the original voyage-4-lite plan — your reasoning confirms it, and the account #2 code-3 path gets dropped.

## Unified plan

| Item | Action |

| 44 rust deps | vectorize → voyage-4-lite → add to the fused set |
| `rust-lang/rust` (code-3 copy) | re-vectorize under voyage-4-lite so it fuses too; retire the code-3 collection |

content.text:
You're right and I was wrong — thank you for pushing. I argued from a general prior ("different models = different vector spaces"), but the **voyage-4 series deliberately breaks that rule.** It's an *industry-first shared embedding space*:

> "All four models produce compatible embeddings that can be used interchangeably… index with voyage-4-large for maximum retrieval quality, then query with any Voyage 4 model… eliminating the need to re-index when switching between models in the series."

The docs confirm it flatly: *"All embeddings created with the 4 series are compatible with each other."* So voyage-4-lite, voyage-4, voyage-4-large, and voyage-4-nano vectors **do** fuse and compare directly. My earlier "lite won't fuse with large" claim was flat wrong for this family.

## What this changes (it simplifies everything)

| Earlier (wrong) assumption | Reality |
|---|---|
| Must re-vectorize the 6 existing lite collections to unify | **No** — they're already in the shared 4-series space, leave them untouched |
| Rust must use the *same* model as the rest to fuse | **No** — embed rust with **any** 4-series model; it fuses with the lite collections regardless |
| 122M lite ceiling is the constraint | **Gone** — use voyage-4-large (~310M) or voyage-4 (~400M) for the rust content; it still fuses with the lite-built collections |

## Corrected plan

- **44 rust deps** → embed with **voyage-4-large** (plenty of tokens, best quality) → new collection → fuses with the existing lite set. ✅
- **`rust-lang/rust`** → re-vectorize under **voyage-4-large** too. This is the one genuinely worth redoing, because its current home is **voyage-code-3**, which is *not* part of the 4-series shared space — that's the real odd-one-out, not lite. Moving it into 4-large folds it into the unified fused corpus and retires the code-3 silo.
- **Existing language + schema/compliance collections** → no change.
- **Server query model** → any 4-series; voyage-4-large for best quality, or lite for cheapest queries — all fuse across every collection.
- **Small code tweak** → add the new rust 4-series collection to `DEFAULT_VOYAGE4_LITE_COLLECTIONS` (that constant is really "the 4-series fused set" now), and drop rust from the code-3 solo profile.

Net: your "put everything in the 4 family" instinct was exactly right, and the shared embedding space means it costs *less* than I framed — no mass re-vectorization, just the rust content on a high-token 4-series tier.

Sources:
- [The Voyage 4 model family: shared embedding space with MoE architecture](https://blog.voyageai.com/2026/01/15/voyage-4/)
- [Announcing New Models and Expanded Availability — Voyage AI](https://blog.voyageai.com/2026/01/15/new-models-and-expanded-availability/)
- [The Voyage 4 Series Now Available — MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/products/updates/the-voyage-4-series-now-available/)

Let me save this so I don't re-derive it wrong later.

The **Voyage 4 series** (`voyage-4-large`, `voyage-4`, `voyage-4-lite`, `voyage-4-nano`) uses an **industry-first shared embedding space**: all four models produce **compatible, interchangeable** embeddings. You can index with one and query with another, and **fuse/cosine-compare vectors across them directly** — no re-indexing, no transformation. (Index bulk with a cheap tier, query with a higher tier, etc.)

Practical consequences for the [[project_mcp_grpc_transport]] / cognitive-mcp RAG corpus:
- The existing `repos_lsp_*_voyage_4_lite` + `repos_specs_docs_voyage_4_lite` collections do NOT need re-vectorizing to unify — they're already in the shared 4-series space.
- New content (e.g. the unvectorized Rust crates, see [[project_rust_crate_vectorization_gap]]) can be embedded with ANY 4-series model (use whichever account/tier has tokens) and it will fuse with the lite-built collections.

Re-do rust-lang/rust under a 4-series model to fold it in.
- All these collections are 1024-dim / Cosine in Qdrant.

I initially (wrongly) asserted "voyage-4-lite won't fuse with voyage-4-large" from a generic embedding-model prior — the user corrected me. The 4-series shared space deliberately breaks that prior. Verify provider specifics, don't assume cross-model incompatibility. See [[feedback_no_unfounded_generalizations]].

input.prompt: List all Voyage embedding models with their specs. For the voyage-4 series (voyage-4-large, voyage-4, voyage-4-lite, voyage-4-nano) and any code-specific models, give: context length, embedding dimensions (default and supported options/Matryoshka), supported output dtypes (float, int8, binary), and any statement about the shared embedding space / cross-model compatibility within the 4 series. Also note which models are recommended for code retrieval and whether voyage-code-3 or a voyage-4 code variant exists.

content.content:
# Voyage Embedding Models Overview

## Voyage-4 Series (General Purpose)

| Model | Context Length | Dimensions | Description |
|-------|---|---|---|
| **voyage-4-large** | 32,000 tokens | 1024 (default), 256, 512, 2048 | Best general-purpose and multilingual retrieval quality |
| **voyage-4** | 32,000 tokens | 1024 (default), 256, 512, 2048 | Optimized for general-purpose and multilingual retrieval |
| **voyage-4-lite** | 32,000 tokens | 1024 (default), 256, 512, 2048 | Optimized for latency and cost |
| **voyage-4-nano** | 32,000 tokens | 512 (default), 128, 256 | Open-weight model (Hugging Face) |

### Voyage-4 Series Compatibility
- **All embeddings created with the 4 series are compatible with each other** (shared embedding space)
- Supports Matryoshka dimensionality reduction (256, 512, 1024, 2048 options)
- Output dtypes: The documentation does not explicitly specify supported output dtypes (float, int8, binary)

## Code-Specific Models

| Model | Context Length | Dimensions | Notes |
|-------|---|---|---|
| **voyage-code-3** | 32,000 tokens | 1024 (default), 256, 512, 2048 | Optimized for code retrieval and documentation; supports Matryoshka |
| **voyage-code-2** | 16,000 tokens | 1536 | Previous generation (legacy); 17% better than alternatives |

**Recommendation**: Use **voyage-code-3** for code retrieval. No voyage-4 code variant exists; instead, voyage-code-3 is the dedicated model for this domain.

## Other Specialized Models

- **voyage-finance-2**: 32,000 tokens, 1024 dimensions (finance RAG)
- **voyage-law-2**: 16,000 tokens, 1024 dimensions (legal RAG)
- **voyage-context-4**: 120,000 tokens, 1024/256/512/2048 dimensions (contextualized chunk embeddings)
- **voyage-multimodal-3.5**: 32,000 tokens, 1024/256/512/2048 dimensions (text, image, video)

The documentation does not provide explicit details about output dtype support (float, int8, binary) across these models.

content.text:
That doc nails down the last details and confirms the plan — with two nuances worth stating explicitly:

## Confirmed
- **voyage-4 series shared embedding space** — all of 4-large/4/4-lite/4-nano compatible. ✅
- **32K context** on every 4-series model — plenty for code chunks (your chunks are ~80 lines / ~2KB).
- **Matryoshka dims** 256/512/1024/2048 — but to fuse, everything must be at the **same** dimension. Your existing collections are **1024**, which is the default for 4-large/4/4-lite. So pin new rust embeddings to **1024**.

## Two nuances this doc surfaces

1. **There is no voyage-4 *code* variant.** "Use voyage-code-3 for code retrieval. No voyage-4 code variant exists." 1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Export rust-analyzer document symbols for rust-lang/rust as JSONL.
4	
5	This uses the same LSP backend configured for Kiro in:
6	  /home/jeremy/git/repos/rust-lang/rust/.kiro/settings/lsp.json
7	
8	Output records are one symbol per line:
9	  {"file_path": "...", "name": "...", "kind": 12, "line_start": 1, ...}
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import argparse
15	import json
16	import os
17	import queue
18	import subprocess
19	import sys
20	import threading
21	import time
22	from pathlib import Path
23	from typing import Any
24	
25	
26	GIT_ROOT = Path("/home/jeremy/git")
27	REPO_ROOT = GIT_ROOT / "repos" / "rust-lang" / "rust"
28	DEFAULT_OUT = GIT_ROOT / "lsp" / "rust-lang-rust-symbols.jsonl"
29	KIRO_LSP_CONFIG = REPO_ROOT / ".kiro" / "settings" / "lsp.json"
30	
31	
32	def uri_for(path: Path) -> str:
33	    return path.resolve().as_uri()
34	
35	
36	def git_files(repo_root: Path, limit: int | None = None) -> list[str]:
37	    files = subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files", "*.rs"], cwd=repo_root, text=True).splitlines()
38	    return files[:limit] if limit else files
39	
40	
41	class LspClient:
42	    def __init__(self, command: list[str], cwd: Path):
43	        self.proc = subprocess.Popen(
44	            command,
45	            cwd=cwd,
46	            stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
47	            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
48	            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
49	            text=False,
50	        )
51	        self.next_id = 1
52	        self.responses: dict[int, Any] = {}
53	        self.notifications: queue.Queue[Any] = queue.Queue()
54	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
55	        self._reader = threading.Thread(target=self._read_loop, daemon=True)
56	        self._reader.start()
57	        self._stderr = threading.Thread(target=self._stderr_loop, daemon=True)
58	        self._stderr.start()
59	
60	    def _stderr_loop(self) -> None:
61	        assert self.proc.stderr is not None
62	        for raw in self.proc.stderr:
63	            line = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").rstrip()
64	            if line:
65	                print(f"rust-analyzer: {line}", file=sys.stderr)
66	
67	    def _read_loop(self) -> None:
68	        assert self.proc.stdout is not None
69	        while True:
70	            headers: dict[str, str] = {}
71	            while True:
72	                line = self.proc.stdout.readline()
73	                if not line:
74	                    return
75	                if line in (b"\r\n", b"\n"):
76	                    break
77	                key, value = line.decode("ascii", errors="replace").split(":", 1)
78	                headers[key.lower()] = value.strip()
79	            length = int(headers.get("content-length", "0"))
80	            if length <= 0:
81	                continue
82	            body = self.proc.stdout.read(length)
83	            msg = json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"))
84	            if "id" in msg:
85	                with self._lock:
86	                    self.responses[msg["id"]] = msg
87	            else:
88	                self.notifications.put(msg)
89	
90	    def send(self, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
91	        assert self.proc.stdin is not None
92	        body = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
93	        header = f"Content-Length: {len(body)}\r\n\r\n".encode("ascii")
94	        self.proc.stdin.write(header + body)
95	        self.proc.stdin.flush()
96	
97	    def request(self, method: str, params: Any = None, timeout: float = 120.0) -> Any:
98	        req_id = self.next_id
99	        self.next_id += 1
100	        payload = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": req_id, "method": method}
101	        if params is not None:
102	            payload["params"] = params
103	        self.send(payload)
104	        deadline = time.time() + timeout
105	        while time.time() < deadline:
106	            with self._lock:
107	                msg = self.responses.pop(req_id, None)
108	            if msg is not None:
109	                if "error" in msg:
110	                    raise RuntimeError(f"{method} failed: {msg['error']}")
111	                return msg.get("result")
112	            if self.proc.poll() is not None:
113	                raise RuntimeError(f"LSP process exited with {self.proc.returncode}")
114	            time.sleep(0.05)
115	        raise TimeoutError(f"{method} timed out")
116	
117	    def notify(self, method: str, params: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
118	        self.send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params})
119	
120	    def close(self) -> None:
121	        try:
122	            self.request("shutdown", None, timeout=10)
123	            self.notify("exit", {})
124	        finally:
125	            try:
126	                self.proc.terminate()
127	            except ProcessLookupError:
128	                pass
129	
130	
131	def flatten_symbols(symbols: list[dict[str, Any]], rel_path: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
132	    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
133	
134	    def walk(items: list[dict[str, Any]], parent: str = "") -> None:
135	        for item in items:
136	            name = item.get("name", "")
137	            qualified = f"{parent}::{name}" if parent and name else name
138	            rng = item.get("range") or item.get("selectionRange") or {}
139	            start = rng.get("start", {})
140	            end = rng.get("end", {})
141	            if name and start and end:
142	                out.append({
143	                    "file_path": rel_path,
144	                    "name": name,
145	                    "qualified_name": qualified,
146	                    "kind": item.get("kind"),
147	                    "line_start": int(start.get("line", 0)) + 1,
148	                    "line_end": int(end.get("line", 0)) + 1,
149	                    "character_start": int(start.get("character", 0)),
150	                    "character_end": int(end.get("character", 0)),
151	                })
152	            children = item.get("children") or []
153	            if children:
154	                walk(children, qualified)
155	
156	    walk(symbols)
157	    return out
158	
159	
160	def load_command() -> list[str]:
161	    if KIRO_LSP_CONFIG.exists():
162	        data = json.loads(KIRO_LSP_CONFIG.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
163	        rust = data.get("languages", {}).get("rust", {})
164	        command = rust.get("command") or "rust-analyzer"
165	        args = rust.get("args") or []
166	        return [command, *args]
167	    return ["rust-analyzer"]
168	
169	
170	def main() -> int:
171	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
172	    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT)
173	    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="Limit files for testing.")
174	    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=180.0)
175	    args = parser.parse_args()
176	
177	    files = git_files(REPO_ROOT, args.limit or None)
178	    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
179	
180	    client = LspClient(load_command(), REPO_ROOT)
181	    try:
182	        client.request("initialize", {
183	            "processId": os.getpid(),
184	            "rootUri": uri_for(REPO_ROOT),
185	            "workspaceFolders": [{"uri": uri_for(REPO_ROOT), "name": "rust"}],
186	            "capabilities": {
187	                "textDocument": {
188	                    "documentSymbol": {
189	                        "hierarchicalDocumentSymbolSupport": True,
190	                    }
191	                }
192	            },
193	        }, timeout=args.timeout)
194	        client.notify("initialized", {})
195	
196	        count = 0
197	        with args.out.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
198	            for idx, rel_path in enumerate(files, 1):
199	                abs_path = REPO_ROOT / rel_path
200	                text = abs_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
201	                uri = uri_for(abs_path)
202	                client.notify("textDocument/didOpen", {
203	                    "textDocument": {
204	                        "uri": uri,
205	                        "languageId": "rust",
206	                        "version": 1,
207	                        "text": text,
208	                    }
209	                })
210	                try:
211	                    symbols = client.request(
212	                        "textDocument/documentSymbol",
213	                        {"textDocument": {"uri": uri}},
214	                        timeout=args.timeout,
215	                    ) or []
216	                    for record in flatten_symbols(symbols, rel_path):
217	                        f.write(json.dumps(record, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")
218	                        count += 1
219	                finally:
220	                    client.notify("textDocument/didClose", {"textDocument": {"uri": uri}})
221	                if idx % 250 == 0:
222	                    print(f"processed {idx}/{len(files)} files, {count} symbols", file=sys.stderr)
223	        print(f"wrote {count} symbols to {args.out}")
224	        return 0
225	    finally:
226	        client.close()
227	
228	
229	if __name__ == "__main__":
230	    raise SystemExit(main())

249	def chunk_text(
250	    text: str,
251	    *,
252	    chunk_chars: int,
253	    overlap_chars: int,
254	) -> Iterator[tuple[str, int, int]]:
255	    if len(text) <= chunk_chars:
256	        yield text, 0, len(text)
257	        return
258	
259	    start = 0
260	    while start < len(text):
261	        hard_end = min(start + chunk_chars, len(text))
262	        end = hard_end
263	        if hard_end < len(text):
264	            newline = text.rfind("\n\n", start + chunk_chars // 2, hard_end)
265	            if newline != -1:
266	                end = newline + 2
267	            else:
268	                newline = text.rfind("\n", start + chunk_chars // 2, hard_end)
269	                if newline != -1:
270	                    end = newline + 1
271	
272	        chunk = text[start:end].strip()
273	        if chunk:
274	            yield chunk, start, end
275	
276	        if end >= len(text):
277	            break
278	        start = max(0, end - overlap_chars)

281	def load_lsp_symbols(path: Path | None) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
282	    if path is None or not path.exists():
283	        return {}
284	    by_file: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
285	    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
286	        if not line.strip():
287	            continue
288	        record = json.loads(line)
289	        by_file.setdefault(record["file_path"], []).append(record)
290	    for records in by_file.values():
291	        records.sort(key=lambda rec: (rec.get("line_start", 0), rec.get("line_end", 0)))
292	    return by_file

295	def lsp_symbol_ranges(
296	    text: str,
297	    symbols: list[dict],
298	    *,
299	    chunk_chars: int,
300	) -> list[tuple[str, int, int, str]]:
301	    offsets = line_offsets(text)
302	    ranges: list[tuple[str, int, int, str]] = []
303	    for symbol in symbols:
304	        start = char_for_line(offsets, int(symbol.get("line_start") or 1))
305	        end_line = max(int(symbol.get("line_end") or symbol.get("line_start") or 1), int(symbol.get("line_start") or 1))
306	        end = char_for_line(offsets, end_line + 1)
307	        if end <= start:
308	            continue
309	        name = str(symbol.get("qualified_name") or symbol.get("name") or "")
310	        segment = text[start:end].strip()
311	        if not segment:
312	            continue
313	        if len(segment) <= chunk_chars:
314	            ranges.append((segment, start, end, name))
315	        else:
316	            for sub, sub_start, sub_end in chunk_text(segment, chunk_chars=chunk_chars, overlap_chars=0):
317	                ranges.append((sub, start + sub_start, start + sub_end, name))
318	    return ranges

321	def make_chunks(
322	    repo_root: Path,
323	    files: Iterable[str],
324	    *,
325	    include_fixtures: bool,
326	    chunk_chars: int,
327	    overlap_chars: int,
328	    max_file_bytes: int,
329	    lsp_symbols: dict[str, list[dict]] | None = None,
330	) -> Iterator[Chunk]:
331	    lsp_symbols = lsp_symbols or {}
332	    for rel_path in files:
333	        if should_skip_path(rel_path, include_fixtures):
334	            continue
335	
336	        abs_path = repo_root / rel_path
337	        text = read_text(abs_path, max_file_bytes)
338	        if not text or not text.strip():
339	            continue
340	
341	        encoded = text.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")
342	        file_sha = hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()
343	        component = component_for(rel_path)
344	        crate = crate_for(rel_path)
345	        language = language_for(rel_path)
346	
347	        if language == "rust" and rel_path in lsp_symbols:
348	            ranges = lsp_symbol_ranges(text, lsp_symbols[rel_path], chunk_chars=chunk_chars)
349	        else:
350	            ranges = [
351	                (chunk, start, end, "")
352	                for chunk, start, end in chunk_text(text, chunk_chars=chunk_chars, overlap_chars=overlap_chars)
353	            ]
354	
355	        for idx, (chunk, start, end, lsp_symbol) in enumerate(ranges):
356	            symbol = lsp_symbol or (nearest_rust_symbol(text[:start]) if language == "rust" else "")
357	            yield Chunk(
358	                text=chunk,
359	                rel_path=rel_path,
360	                abs_path=abs_path,
361	                chunk_index=idx,
362	                line_start=line_number_at(text, start),
363	                line_end=line_number_at(text, end),
364	                char_start=start,
365	                char_end=end,
366	                file_sha256=file_sha,
367	                symbol=symbol,
368	                component=component,
369	                crate=crate,
370	                language=language,
371	            )

622	def ingest(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
623	    if not os.environ.get("VOYAGE_API_KEY"):
624	        raise SystemExit("VOYAGE_API_KEY is not set.")
625	
626	    voyageai, QdrantClient, Distance, PointStruct, VectorParams = import_clients()
627	    voyage_client = voyageai.Client()
628	    qdrant = QdrantClient(url=args.qdrant_url, timeout=args.qdrant_timeout)
629	
630	    ensure_collection(
631	        qdrant,
632	        args.collection,
633	        args.dimension,
634	        Distance,
635	        VectorParams,
636	        args.recreate,
637	    )
638	    create_payload_indexes(qdrant, args.collection)
639	
640	    repo_meta = git_metadata(REPO_ROOT)
641	    files = git_files(REPO_ROOT)
642	    lsp_symbol_path = DEFAULT_LSP_SYMBOLS if args.use_default_lsp_symbols else args.lsp_symbols
643	    lsp_symbols = load_lsp_symbols(lsp_symbol_path)
644	    if lsp_symbols:
645	        logging.info("Loaded LSP symbols for %s files from %s", len(lsp_symbols), lsp_symbol_path)
646	    chunks = make_chunks(
647	        REPO_ROOT,
648	        files,
649	        include_fixtures=args.include_rust_test_fixtures,
650	        chunk_chars=args.chunk_chars,
651	        overlap_chars=args.overlap_chars,
652	        max_file_bytes=args.max_file_bytes,
653	        lsp_symbols=lsp_symbols,
654	    )
655	
656	    total_chunks = 0
657	    skipped_existing = 0
658	    total_estimated_tokens = 0
659	    started = time.time()
660	
661	    def qdrant_upsert_with_retry(points: list, depth: int = 0) -> None:
662	        try:
663	            qdrant.upsert(
664	                collection_name=args.collection,
665	                points=points,
666	                wait=False,
667	                timeout=args.qdrant_timeout,
668	            )
669	            return
670	        except Exception as exc:
671	            if is_transient_qdrant_error(exc) and depth < 8:
672	                sleep_s = min(120, 5 * (2 ** depth))
673	                logging.warning("Qdrant upsert transient failure; sleeping %ss: %s", sleep_s, exc)
674	                time.sleep(sleep_s)
675	                qdrant_upsert_with_retry(points, depth + 1)
676	                return
677	            raise

679	    def existing_ids(batch: list[Chunk], depth: int = 0) -> set[str]:
680	        if not args.skip_existing:
681	            return set()
682	        ids = [point_id(chunk, repo_meta.get("commit", "")) for chunk in batch]
683	        try:
684	            points = qdrant.retrieve(
685	                collection_name=args.collection,
686	                ids=ids,
687	                with_payload=False,
688	                with_vectors=False,
689	                timeout=args.qdrant_timeout,
690	            )
691	        except Exception as exc:
692	            if is_transient_qdrant_error(exc) and depth < 5:
693	                sleep_s = min(60, 3 * (2 ** depth))
694	                logging.warning("Qdrant existing-id check failed; sleeping %ss: %s", sleep_s, exc)
695	                time.sleep(sleep_s)
696	                return existing_ids(batch, depth + 1)
697	            raise
698	        return {str(point.id) for point in points}
699	
700	    def upsert_batch(batch: list[Chunk], depth: int = 0) -> int:
701	        nonlocal total_chunks, skipped_existing
702	        existing = existing_ids(batch)
703	        if existing:
704	            before = len(batch)
705	            batch = [
706	                chunk
707	                for chunk in batch
708	                if point_id(chunk, repo_meta.get("commit", "")) not in existing
709	            ]
710	            skipped_existing += before - len(batch)
711	            if not batch:
712	                return 0
713	
714	        try:
715	            result = voyage_client.embed(
716	                [chunk.text for chunk in batch],
717	                model=args.model,
718	                input_type="document",
719	                output_dimension=args.dimension,
720	            )
721	        except Exception as exc:
722	            if is_batch_too_large_error(exc) and len(batch) > 1:
723	                mid = len(batch) // 2
724	                logging.warning(
725	                    "Splitting oversized Voyage batch of %s chunks at depth %s: %s",
726	                    len(batch),
727	                    depth,
728	                    exc,
729	                )
730	                return upsert_batch(batch[:mid], depth + 1) + upsert_batch(batch[mid:], depth + 1)
731	            if is_rate_limit_error(exc):
732	                sleep_s = min(900, 30 * (2 ** min(depth, 5)))
733	                logging.warning("Voyage rate limit hit; sleeping %ss before retry: %s", sleep_s, exc)
734	                time.sleep(sleep_s)
735	                return upsert_batch(batch, depth + 1)
736	            raise
737	
738	        points = [
739	            PointStruct(
740	                id=point_id(chunk, repo_meta.get("commit", "")),
741	                vector=embedding,
742	                payload=payload_for(chunk, repo_meta),
743	            )
744	            for chunk, embedding in zip(batch, result.embeddings)
745	        ]
746	        qdrant_upsert_with_retry(points)
747	        total_chunks += len(batch)
748	        return len(batch)
749	
750	    for batch in batched(chunks, args.batch_size):
751	        if args.skip_existing:
752	            existing = existing_ids(batch)
753	            if existing:
754	                before = len(batch)
755	                batch = [
756	                    chunk
757	                    for chunk in batch
758	                    if point_id(chunk, repo_meta.get("commit", "")) not in existing
759	                ]
760	                skipped_existing += before - len(batch)
761	                if not batch:
762	                    if skipped_existing % (args.batch_size * 100) == 0:
763	                        logging.info("Skipped %s existing chunks", skipped_existing)
764	                    continue
765	
766	        batch_tokens = sum(estimate_tokens(chunk.text) for chunk in batch)
767	        total_estimated_tokens += batch_tokens
768	        if total_estimated_tokens > args.max_estimated_tokens:
769	            raise SystemExit(
770	                f"Estimated token limit exceeded: {total_estimated_tokens} > {args.max_estimated_tokens}. "
771	                "Raise --max-estimated-tokens if this is intentional."
772	            )
773	
774	        upsert_batch(batch)
775	        if total_chunks % (args.batch_size * 10) == 0:
776	            elapsed = max(1.0, time.time() - started)
777	            logging.info(
778	                "Upserted %s chunks, skipped %s existing, estimated %s tokens, %.1f chunks/sec",
779	                total_chunks,
780	                skipped_existing,
781	                total_estimated_tokens,
782	                total_chunks / elapsed,
783	            )
784	
785	    logging.info(
786	        "Complete: upserted %s chunks, skipped %s existing, estimated %s tokens into %s",
787	        total_chunks,
788	        skipped_existing,
789	        total_estimated_tokens,
790	        args.collection,
791	    )
792	    return 0
793	
794	
795	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
796	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
797	    parser.add_argument("--repo-root", type=Path, default=REPO_ROOT)
798	    parser.add_argument("--repo-list", type=Path, default=SOLO_LIST)
799	    parser.add_argument("--qdrant-url", default="http://localhost:6333")
800	    parser.add_argument("--qdrant-timeout", type=int, default=120)
801	    parser.add_argument("--collection", default=DEFAULT_COLLECTION)
802	    parser.add_argument("--model", default=DEFAULT_MODEL)
803	    parser.add_argument("--dimension", type=int, default=DEFAULT_DIMENSION)
804	    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE)
805	    parser.add_argument("--chunk-chars", type=int, default=DEFAULT_CHUNK_CHARS)
806	    parser.add_argument("--overlap-chars", type=int, default=DEFAULT_OVERLAP_CHARS)
807	    parser.add_argument("--max-file-bytes", type=int, default=DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_BYTES)
808	    parser.add_argument("--max-estimated-tokens", type=int, default=DEFAULT_MAX_ESTIMATED_TOKENS)
809	    parser.add_argument("--include-rust-test-fixtures", action="store_true")
810	    parser.add_argument("--lsp-symbols", type=Path, default=None)
811	    parser.add_argument("--use-default-lsp-symbols", action="store_true")
812	    parser.add_argument("--skip-existing", action="store_true")
813	    parser.add_argument("--recreate", action="store_true")
814	    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
815	    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
816	    return parser.parse_args()
817	
818	
819	def validate_scope(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
820	    if args.repo_root.resolve() != REPO_ROOT.resolve():
821	        raise SystemExit(f"This script is scoped to {REPO_ROOT}; got {args.repo_root}")
822	    if args.repo_list.exists():
823	        repos = [
824	            line.strip()
825	            for line in args.repo_list.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
826	            if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("#")
827	        ]
828	        if repos != ["rust-lang/rust"]:
829	            raise SystemExit(f"{args.repo_list} must contain only rust-lang/rust for this solo run.")
830	    if not args.repo_root.is_dir():
831	        raise SystemExit(f"Missing repo root: {args.repo_root}")
832

834	def main() -> int:
